transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-01-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Mateo Ruiz (Redwood); Priya Kumar, Daniel Cho, Sarah Lin (Granite Mutual)
Links mentioned: https://redwood.ai/security-whitepaper.pdf, https://redwood.ai/soc2-report (placeholder)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Granite Mutual is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing document summarization and underwriting-assist workflows. Primary constraints are EU data residency for EU customers, HIPAA overlap for a small vertical product, and financial services auditability. They require tenant isolation, customer-managed KMS option, and strict log redaction/retention controls. Team expressed interest in a pilot on Dedicated with potential move to Private for regulatory proofing.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Lena from Redwood, I run the AE for this region. Quick intros?
[00:12] Priya: Hi this is Priya, head of compliance at Granite Mutual. We're mostly here to understand data boundaries and how logs and keys are handled.
[00:20] Daniel: Daniel, CTO. We're re-evaluating inference vendors and want to map hosting options to our regulatory needs.
[00:26] Sarah: Sarah, platform eng, I'll be the implementer if we move forward.
[00:31] Mateo: Mateo from Redwood's solutions engineering, I can take us through operational details and keystore patterns.
[00:36] Lena: Great. Agenda — quick qualification, then Mateo will go through how Redwood supports hosted / dedicated / private, especially keys and logs; leave time for Q&A and next steps.

[00:58] Priya: High level questions — for EU customers we must ensure no cross-border egress and audit proof logs. Can Redwood guarantee region lock for logs and inference?
[01:10] Mateo: Short answer: yes, we have region-locking and tenancy isolation options. That comes in two ways — hosted with region pinning and dedicated pools in a region, and then private deployments inside a VPC or on-prem for the strictest control. For hosted we can restrict data residency to a region and produce audit trails, however in EU-regulated scenarios most customers prefer Dedicated or Private because it reduces cross-tenant surface.
[01:42] Priya: Is there any routing to US for model service or telemetry? We can't have telemetry that contains cleartext PII leave EU.
[01:50] Mateo: Our control plane (for Redwood Hosted) is multi-region aware, but default telemetry is scrubbed. We also offer an option for customer-managed telemetry — either send logs to your S3 in-region or we can forward to a SIEM endpoint inside your VPC. For Private deployments the control plane is in-customer environment and telemetry stays there.

[02:18] Daniel: On keys — we have strict key residency. We run our own KMS (Cloud HSM) in region. Can Redwood use customer-managed KMS?
[02:27] Mateo: Yes — customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported. For Dedicated we can integrate with your cloud KMS via an enclave-style flow, and for Private you'd run the keystore entirely in your network. There is a routing diagram I'll send that shows key exchange, re-encryption and tokenization.
[02:48] Sarah: What about model weights? Some compliance folks assume model weights are a copy of customer data — that isn't our architecture but they want to be explicit.
[02:58] Lena: Good point — we clarify that model weights are not revised by inference requests; we don't perform fine-tuning with customer data unless explicitly configured for a training product. Typical inference requests do not change model weights.

[03:20] Priya: Logging retention — our legal team requires 7 years for certain transaction logs, but we only want request identifiers and redacted metadata stored long-term. Can you support redaction at source and variable retention per log type?
[03:36] Mateo: We do. Redwood Console supports log classification: you can configure retention per log channel (raw transcripts, request metadata, billing tokens). For Hosted, we can apply automated PII redaction rules at ingestion, but for the highest assurance we recommend Dedicated + customer-side pre-ingest scrubbing. We also support legal-hold exports and can truncate transcript bodies while retaining hashes for audit.
[04:05] Daniel: How deterministic is the redaction? Do you provide reproducible hashing so we can link redacted content to an original if necessary?
[04:14] Mateo: We provide SHA-256 hashes for artifacts to enable integrity checks; redaction uses configurable regex and ML-based PII detectors. There is a small chance of false negatives with ML detectors, so for regulated workloads we often combine pattern rules + an allowlist/denylist.

[04:40] Sarah: Network-wise, if we choose Dedicated, do we get a VPC peering or dedicated private link? We maintain strict egress rules in our VPC.
[04:50] Mateo: For Dedicated we can do VPC peering, PrivateLink, or customer-managed transit. For Private on-prem, there is no outbound egress to Redwood's control plane unless you opt in; we ship a private control plane that you host. We'll share the diagrams.

[05:10] Priya: HIPAA overlap — one of our products is in health finance, data is de-ID'd but still considered PHI in context. Can Redwood provide HIPAA BAAs?
[05:20] Lena: Redwood offers HIPAA support and BAA options on Private deployments and some Dedicated contracts; we'll need to qualify the exact data flows. I'll flag that to our legal team.

[05:36] Daniel: Performance concern — if we lock to EU region and use customer KMS, does latency to KMS for key unwrap degrade token throughput significantly?
[05:47] Mateo: There is a small additional RTT on first token unwrap per session; however we can cache decrypted keys in a secure enclave (or a local HSM session) to amortize that. For high-throughput flows we use long-lived session keys with short rotation windows to balance security and latency. We'll share benchmarking numbers.

[06:12] Priya: Audit evidence — we need a clear trail for who accessed what and when, plus the content lineage for model inputs/outputs. Is that part of the console?
[06:22] Mateo: Yes, Console has per-request traces, including requester identity, model version, route, token counts, latency, and optional payload snapshots depending on retention policy. For compliance we can provide redacted snapshots or hashes only. We also provide signed PDFs of audit reports on request.

[06:45] Daniel: Competitor question — some vendors say they do "in-region sandboxing" but actually the control plane is global. How does Redwood differ?
[06:55] Lena: We differentiate by offering a Private control plane and dedicated regional pools. Our hosted product can be configured for region pinning but if you need zero cross-region control plane traffic we recommend Private. Also we document data paths in the security pack we'll share.

[07:10] Sarah: About logs — our retention policy requires metadata for 7 years but transcripts only 1 year, can you set per-channel retention?
[07:20] Mateo: Yes, per-channel retention is supported. You can export older metadata to cold storage in-region. We also support redaction rules run at ingestion to avoid storing PII in transcripts at all.

[07:40] Priya: Legal hold — if there's a litigation hold, we may need to retain certain transcripts beyond normal retention. How fast can you switch retention and provide export?
[07:52] Mateo: Legal-hold switches can be applied retroactively for preserved artifacts; we can export preserved items on demand. The export process depends on size — small sets can be generated in hours, larger collections may take longer.

[08:07] Daniel: Encryption in transit and at rest — standard? Are there FIPS options?
[08:14] Mateo: TLS 1.2+/1.3 in transit, AES-256 at rest. For FIPS we can support FIPS-compliant HSMs in the customer-managed keystore flow.

[08:30] Priya: Are PII detectors auditable? We may want to know what rule matched.
[08:36] Mateo: We log rule hits and classifier confidence scores; you can also configure deterministic regex checks that are fully auditable. For ML classifiers we log the classifier id and version so you can reproduce.

[08:55] Priya: If we do a pilot, what's the minimum scope? We prefer a small Dedicated pool in eu-west-1 to start with underwriting docs turned on in redaction mode.
[09:05] Lena: That's a common pattern — Dedicated pilot in-region for 6–12 weeks, focused on a subset of traffic. We'll provide a template SLA and run a smoke test and a privacy/pen test checklist.

[09:25] Daniel: SLA and uptime — we need 99.9 for this product. Is that available on Dedicated?
[09:31] Lena: Yes, Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime guarantees; exact numbers are contract dependent. We'll include the SLA matrix in the package.

[09:42] Priya: We're also interested in how Redwood handles retraining/feedback loops. If our agents use model-assisted labeling, is that data retained?
[09:52] Mateo: Only if you opt in to use our fine-tuning or feedback ingestion. Default inference doesn't persist training data. If you do opt in, we have consent and isolation controls and you can choose whether that data is stored in your tenancy.

[10:10] Sarah: A technical edge case — we do cross-border umbrella entities, where a EU subsidiary's logs are ingested by a central SIEM in the US for analytics. That is a no for some customers. Can Redwood route logs separately per tenant?
[10:23] Mateo: Yes, routing is per-tenant. You can have per-tenant sinks and per-region retention rules; for hubs that need cross-region analytics we suggest using aggregated non-PII metrics exported to the US while keeping raw artifacts in-region.

[10:42] Priya: I heard about model-variant fallbacks — if primary model is temporarily unavailable and you fallback to a cheaper or external model, does data route change? This is a risk for residency.
[10:53] Mateo: We have routing policies. You can configure strict no-fallback outside region; fallback is an opt-in policy that can be region-aware. We'll make sure rollback/fallback policies are explicit in the rollout config.

[11:10] Daniel: Anything else from our side before we go deeper?
[11:15] Priya: Just that whatever you send, we need artifact-level evidence for the security review. SOC2 plus deployment diagrams plus PII redaction acceptance tests.
[11:24] Lena: Understood. We'll send the pack and propose dates for the SE deep dive. Mateo, can you run the draft keystore and log routing deck?
[11:31] Mateo: Yup, I'll prepare that and include latency bench numbers for KMS unwrap, plus a sample retention config.

[11:40] (brief crosstalk)
[11:45] Sarah: One minor question — for dedicated pools, is the model catalog the same as hosted? We need certain model families approved.
[11:53] Mateo: Yes, model catalog parity is maintained; for Private you can also bring custom model artifacts if you need. Note: third-party model licensing can affect distribution.

[12:10] Priya: Lastly, access control — we require RBAC and SSO with SCIM provisioning.
[12:17] Lena: Redwood supports SSO via SAML/OIDC and SCIM for provisioning. RBAC is customizable per-team + per-route. We'll include admin/user roles in the admin guide.

[12:35] Daniel: Good. I think the next step is the security pack and then a deep technical session around keystore and pilots.
[12:43] Lena: Great. I'll summarize next steps in an email after the call. Thanks everyone.

[13:00] End of recording.

Notes on transcription quality: background noise at minute 9 and a small glitch at 00:58 where "region pinning" was transcribed as "region pending". Some proper nouns (e.g., HSM vendor names) were generalized by the auto-transcriber.
